claims.text: Untreated high-performance alloy steel components suffer surface degradation through oxidation, corrosion, and mechanical wear in aggressive high-temperature environments.
Silicon incorporation in an ALD alumina coating enhances adhesion to the steel substrate.
Silicon incorporation creates a graded coating–steel interface.
The engineered ALD process induces beneficial compressive stresses in the coating system.
The induced compressive stresses enhance crack resistance.
The intervention produces a conformal, dense, ultrathin amorphous alumina film.
The alumina film chemically bonds to the steel through a silicon-enhanced graded interface.
Interfacial compressive stress mitigates crack initiation and propagation.
The ALD-grown coating acts as a barrier against oxygen and corrosive agents.
Barrier action by the coating reduces oxidation and chemical degradation.
The nanolaminate structure and induced compressive stresses increase surface hardness.
The nanolaminate structure and induced compressive stresses increase wear resistance.
Silicon doping reduces the coating's defect density.
The coating will improve surface hardness by approximately 30–50% relative to untreated alloy steel.
The coating will improve wear resistance by approximately 30–50% relative to untreated alloy steel.
The coating will provide enhanced oxidation resistance during prolonged exposure.
The coating will provide enhanced corrosion resistance during prolonged exposure.
The coating can remain effective at 500–700°C in oxidizing environments containing SO2 and chloride species, provided adhesion and interface integrity are retained during thermal cycling.
